symbols.name: \(n\)
symbols.def: Half-sample-size index; the experiment observes \(2n\) units.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal H_n(\bar\delta)\)
symbols.def: Truth classes with a uniform learner-class witness at budget \(\bar\delta\).

symbols.name: \(P\)
symbols.def: Generic law in the mean-zero fixed-class model.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0}(F_\mu,F_\pi)\)
symbols.def: Mean-zero full two-nuisance partially linear model for a fixed class pair.

symbols.name: \(\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0,\rm na}(F_\mu,F_\pi)\)
symbols.def: Bounded non-atomic-treatment subclass of \(\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0}(F_\mu,F_\pi)\).

symbols.name: \(\beta(P)\)
symbols.def: Coefficient identified by a law \(P\) in the mean-zero model.

symbols.name: \(\widehat\beta\)
symbols.def: Measurable estimator tailored to the selected fixed truth classes and budgets.

symbols.name: \(\widehat\beta_n\)
symbols.def: An \(n\)-indexed estimator tailored to a selected hard class pair.

symbols.name: \(m_{\rm PL}^{0}(n,\bar\delta_\mu,\bar\delta_\pi)\)
symbols.def: Fixed-class minimax expected absolute risk of the mean-zero full two-nuisance partially linear model.

symbols.name: \(\mathsf U_n\)
symbols.def: Theorem A.1 displayed upper expression in the proposed regime.

symbols.name: \(\mathsf L_n\)
symbols.def: Theorem A.1 displayed lower expression in the proposed regime.

symbols.name: \(F_{\mu,n}\)
symbols.def: Fixed outcome truth class in the \(n\)-th hard witness.

symbols.name: \(F_{\pi,n}\)
symbols.def: Fixed treatment truth class in the \(n\)-th hard witness.

assumptions.condition: A pair \(F,G\subseteq\mathcal T_3\) obeys \(\sup_{f\in F}\inf_{g\in G}\lVert f-g\rVert_{L^2(\nu_d)}\le\delta^{\rm appr}\).
A learner class \(G\subseteq\mathcal T_3\) obeys \(\sup_{\delta>0:\,\delta\ge\delta^{\rm stoc}}\mathcal R_{n,\nu_d}(\delta;\partial G)/(3\delta)\le\delta^{\rm stoc}\).
The \(2n\) observations are independent and identically distributed under \(P\).

definitions.name: Admissible truth classes
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal H_n(\bar\delta)=\{F\subseteq\mathcal T_3:\exists G\subseteq\mathcal T_3,\ \sup_{f\in F}\inf_{g\in G}\lVert f-g\rVert_{L^2(\nu_d)}\le\delta^{\rm appr},\ \sup_{\delta>0:\,\delta\ge\delta^{\rm stoc}}\mathcal R_{n,\nu_d}(\delta;\partial G)/(3\delta)\le\delta^{\rm stoc}\}\), where \(\bar\delta=(\delta^{\rm appr},\delta^{\rm stoc})\).

definitions.name: Mean-zero full two-nuisance partially linear family
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0}(F_\mu,F_\pi)=\{P_{\beta,v,\mu,\pi}^{0}:X\sim\nu_d,\ \mu\in F_\mu,\ \pi\in F_\pi,\ T=\pi(X)+u,\ \mathbb E[u\mid X]=0,\ \mathbb E[u^2\mid X]\equiv v\ge1/3,\ Y=\beta T+\mu(X)+\varepsilon,\ \mathbb E[\varepsilon\mid X,T]=0,\ |\beta|\vee|v|\le3,\ |T|\vee|Y|\le3\}\). This is the mean-zero full two-nuisance PLM consistent with equations (1.1) and (3.2) of \cite{gu2026optimally}.

definitions.name: Bounded non-atomic treatment subclass
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0,\rm na}(F_\mu,F_\pi)=\{P\in\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0}(F_\mu,F_\pi):P(T=t)=0\text{ for every }t\in[-3,3]\}\).

definitions.name: Mean-zero fixed-class minimax risk
definitions.construction: \(m_{\rm PL}^{0}(n,\bar\delta_\mu,\bar\delta_\pi)=\sup_{F_\mu\in\mathcal H_n(\bar\delta_\mu)}\sup_{F_\pi\in\mathcal H_n(\bar\delta_\pi)}\inf_{\widehat\beta}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0}(F_\mu,F_\pi)}\int|\widehat\beta(o_{1:2n})-\beta(P)|\,dP^{\otimes2n}(o_{1:2n})\). The infimum occurs after selection of the fixed class pair, so the estimator may know the truth classes and budgets.

definitions.name: Theorem A.1 displayed benchmarks
definitions.construction: In Appendix A.1 of \cite{gu2026optimally}, the outcome error is denoted \(\varepsilon_Y\), and its condition is \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_Y\mid X,T]=0\). Theorem A.1 displays \(n^{-1/2}+[\delta_\mu^{\rm appr}+(\delta_\mu^{\rm stoc})^2]\wedge[(\delta_\mu^{\rm appr}+\delta_\mu^{\rm stoc})(\delta_\pi^{\rm appr}+\delta_\pi^{\rm stoc})]\) and \(n^{-1/2}+[\delta_\mu^{\rm appr}+(\delta_\mu^{\rm stoc})^2][\delta_\pi^{\rm appr}+(\delta_\pi^{\rm stoc})^2]+(\delta_\mu^{\rm stoc}\wedge\delta_\pi^{\rm stoc})^2\). At the proposed budgets these define \(\mathsf U_n=n^{-1/2}+\min\{s_{\mu,n}^2,s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n}\}\) and \(\mathsf L_n=n^{-1/2}+s_{\mu,n}^2s_{\pi,n}^2+s_{\pi,n}^2\). The paper uses \(2n\) observations, which changes only constants.

statements.statement: For every sequence in \(\mathcal R_n^{\rm asym}\), the displayed expressions satisfy \(\mathsf U_n\asymp s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n}\) and \(\mathsf L_n=o(s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n})\).
statements.justification: This algebra records the separation between the two displayed Appendix A.1 benchmark expressions in the asymmetric regime.
statements.gap: The algebra is comparative context only and does not determine the minimax rate under a rich covariate design.
statements.consumer: It identifies the product scale against which the degenerate-design root-\(n\) order is compared.

statements.statement: For every sequence \((\bar\delta_{\mu,n},\bar\delta_{\pi,n})\in\mathcal R_n^{\rm asym}\), do there exist \(c>0\) and \(N\in\mathbb N\) such that for every \(n\ge N\) one can choose fixed, nonrandom \(F_{\mu,n}\in\mathcal H_n(0,s_{\mu,n})\) and \(F_{\pi,n}\in\mathcal H_n(0,s_{\pi,n})\) for which \(\inf_{\widehat\beta_n}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0,\rm na}(F_{\mu,n},F_{\pi,n})}\int|\widehat\beta_n(o_{1:2n})-\beta(P)|\,dP^{\otimes2n}(o_{1:2n})\ge c s_{\mu,n}s_{\pi,n}\)? Conditional on author confirmation that the \(Y\) in Appendix A.1 is typographical, an affirmative answer strictly tightens Theorem A.1's displayed lower bound and closes its asymmetric branch; without confirmation, it is a closely motivated new experiment rather than a proved tightening of the literal Appendix A.1 risk.
statements.justification: One fixed two-channel truth-class pair is the missing product converse for the mean-zero full two-nuisance PLM.
statements.gap: Theorem A.1's displayed lower expression is below the product scale under its apparent intended mean-zero reading; Jin--Mackey--Syrgkanis and Jin--Syrgkanis study distinct experiments.
statements.consumer: An affirmative answer establishes the missing fixed-class product converse for the mean-zero full two-nuisance PLM; conditional on author confirmation that the \(Y\) in Appendix A.1 is typographical, it strictly tightens Theorem A.1's displayed lower bound and closes its asymmetric branch; without confirmation, it is a closely motivated new experiment rather than a proved tightening of the literal Appendix A.1 risk.

sampling_model.design: The experiment observes \(2n\) independent and identically distributed triples \((X_i,T_i,Y_i)\) from \(P\in\mathcal P_{\rm PL}^{0}(F_\mu,F_\pi)\). The exact-boundary theorem specializes the allowed reference law to \(X_i=x_0\) almost surely.
sampling_model.treatment: \(T=\pi(X)+u\), \(\mathbb E[u\mid X]=0\), and \(\mathbb E[u^2\mid X]\equiv v\ge1/3\); the hard witness restricts further to bounded non-atomic treatment.
sampling_model.overlap: The lower bound \(v\ge1/3\) is the model's overlap analogue.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The estimator is selected after the fixed truth-class pair and may be tailored to the truth classes and budgets.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Appendix A.1 studies the same fixed-class, two-nuisance, 2n-sample experiment and displays nonmatching upper and lower expressions. The present theorem specializes to an allowed degenerate reference law, supplies a covariate-richness obstruction, and does not tighten the displayed lower bound.
Theorems 3.1--3.2 give binary- and Gaussian-treatment lower bounds for supplied nuisance estimates under worst-case quantile loss.
Sequential perturbations yield lower bounds for general linear functionals; its PLM-preserving example concerns expected conditional covariance rather than this coefficient frontier.
The COLT open-problem note identifies variance propagation in structure-agnostic partially linear estimation.

tldr: When \(\nu_d=\delta_{x_0}\), both nuisance functions are constants almost surely and \(\beta(P)=\operatorname{Cov}_P(T,Y)/\operatorname{Var}_P(T)\). An explicit clipped covariance estimator and a bounded non-atomic Le Cam submodel prove the matching minimax order \(m_{\rm PL}^{0}(n,\bar\delta_\mu,\bar\delta_\pi)\asymp n^{-1/2}\) for every budget pair. Thus product-scale behavior cannot hold uniformly over the frozen design class without a quantitative covariate-richness condition. Appendix A.1 of \cite{gu2026optimally} uses the outcome-error subscript \(\varepsilon_Y\); this note makes no source-typo claim and does not tighten its displayed lower bound.

project_justification.gap: Gu, Yin, Cai, and Fan's two-nuisance displays do not determine which covariate designs can sustain a product term, while the frozen core imposes no quantitative richness condition on \(\nu_d\).
project_justification.niche: The note isolates an admissible boundary design on which both nuisance functions collapse to constants and determines the matching root-\(n\) minimax order in the same fixed-class experiment.
project_justification.fill: A full-model covariance upper bound and a bounded non-atomic two-point lower bound prove \(m_{\rm PL}^{0}\asymp n^{-1/2}\) when \(\nu_d=\delta_{x_0}\). This is a covariate-richness obstruction and does not tighten Gu, Yin, Cai, and Fan's displayed lower bound.

related_work: Robinson \cite{robinson1988root} gives the classical root-\(n\) partially linear benchmark, and Chernozhukov et al. \cite{chernozhukov2018dml} give orthogonal-score inference for the coefficient. Gu \cite{gu2025open} identifies variance propagation as an unresolved structure-agnostic issue. Gu, Yin, Cai, and Fan \cite{gu2026optimally}, Appendix A.1, study the same fixed-class, two-nuisance, \(2n\)-sample experiment and display nonmatching upper and lower expressions. The present theorem specializes to an allowed degenerate reference law, supplies a covariate-richness obstruction, and does not tighten their displayed lower bound. Jin, Mackey, and Syrgkanis \cite{jin2025hardnormal} study supplied nuisance estimates and worst-case quantile loss under binary or conditionally Gaussian treatment, while Jin and Syrgkanis \cite{jin2025sharp} develop lower-bound methods for other functionals. Balakrishnan, Kennedy, and Wasserman \cite{balakrishnan2023fundamental} provide the broader structure-agnostic lower-bound perspective.
interpretation: When \(X\) is degenerate, the partially linear model becomes a bounded one-regressor problem with treatment variance bounded away from zero. The nuisance budgets then do not affect the minimax order: the coefficient is a covariance ratio and its risk has matching root-\(n\) upper and lower bounds. Covariate variation is therefore essential to any slower product-scale frontier.
technical_internal_limitation: The verified arXiv:2606.06368v1 source, \texttt{append.tex}, line 18 uses \(\varepsilon_Y\), with \(Y\) as the outcome-error subscript, and imposes \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_Y\mid X,T]=0\). The genuine limitation is that the matching minimax-order theorem treats the degenerate-covariate boundary and does not determine the minimax rate under a separately imposed covariate-richness condition.
honest_scope: The theorem proves the matching root-\(n\) minimax order only for \(\nu_d=\delta_{x_0}\). It shows that a slower product-scale lower bound cannot be uniform over the frozen design class, but it does not establish or refute such a lower bound within a quantitatively rich design subclass. It does not tighten Gu, Yin, Cai, and Fan's displayed lower bound.
